floats.caption: A selected Treasury-bill path that returns within the reported historical limit at its endpoint after an intervening breach. The rule chooses the earliest eligible original evaluation window. Endpoint containment can conceal a peak breach.
Related studies: reported targets, data units and evaluation approaches.
Data and matched six-record peak summaries.
Forecast definitions and executed menus. Codes occur here to connect with the result files. Matched histories and update schedules make the reference explicit.
Long-history short-horizon FX regression under two references and periods. Negative percentages favor regression. Matched gains recur while the rolling-reference direction changes.

Saved short-horizon FX learning curves on the original evaluation period. The methods retain distinct original penalty menus, and every tested history is shown against its own matched historical headroom. This retrospective comparison does not identify a universally optimal history.

Weekly evidence across the original main comparison, added panel and earlier-period comparisons. Counts refer to related tasks rather than independent dealers. Stronger regularization narrows losses while leaving substantial failures.
CFTC dealer-category futures: relative loss versus matched historical headroom (\%). All 17 selected literal contract codes are retained.

Expanded-menu regression relative loss versus matched historical headroom for every eligible CFTC contract. Columns separate histories; code order follows the fixed open-interest ranking. Positive values mean higher regression loss.

Signed decomposition of regression excess loss against matched historical headroom, with selection in blue, the finite-menu diagnostic gap in orange, and actual excess as black dots. Crosses retain unavailable comparisons; the text focuses on short-history weekly cells while all planned comparisons remain plotted.
Full-regression excess loss versus matched historical headroom under longer validation. Entries are source medians in percent; the final column counts selections of the intercept-only limit.
Full-regression relative excess loss (\%) at alternative quantile levels. Positive values favor matched historical headroom; NA retains any failed required comparison.

Fixed reserve and breach-charge regions with the exceedance coefficient held at unity. Color shows the fraction of related comparisons where the stated conditional procedure costs less than corrected historical headroom, with each source group retaining its own histories and horizons. These are descriptive fractions; all comparisons are complete, and the lower and upper fractions coincide.

Ordinary regression and the benchmark-default protocol relative to matched historical headroom. Every planned comparison is complete: 34 CFTC, 26 New York Fed and two FX cases; points retain each outcome, including large losses. Separate vertical scales preserve each source's distribution without pooling native exposure units.
Original increment-autoregression simulation, unchanged. Serial persistence here concerns increments, not fitted position levels.
All corrected primary cases. Mean-reverting level rates are conservative in these finite cases; the negative-increment result must also be retained.
All secondary anchor and conditional-threshold sensitivities. Conditional and marginal endpoint calibration remain distinct.
Every original-cell endpoint plug-in comparison. A population bound does not imply a lower empirical pinball score.
All separate endpoint-plug-in working-reference contrasts. Adverse score comparisons remain alongside lower-breach reports.
Complete original autoregressive replay comparison. Lower scores can accompany more strict breaches.
Complete ordinary-rank ablation. Lower empirical reports increase breach occasions and need not improve score.
The four fixed headline comparisons. The longer-horizon FX result is sensitive to error weights.
Complete panel, first half. Additional regularization leaves substantial adverse cases.
Complete panel, second half. The enlarged penalty menu is not uniformly better than historical rules.
Every additional-panel endpoint-plug-in result. Fewer breaches do not guarantee a better score.
Every earlier-period minimum-loss and one-standard-error comparison. The one-standard-error rule misses the recorded success conditions.
All non-complete fixed-rule report rows. Failed mandatory candidates remain failures.
Complete delayed-wrapper and headroom-recursion inventory. Two long-horizon wrapper cells remain unavailable.
Every paired wrapper comparison. Calibration adjustment preserves the long-history short-horizon FX score gain but does not produce universal dominance.
All original-cell combination comparisons. A report combination can outperform one constituent while losing to the other.
Complete combination counts including the added panel. Missing median constituents remain NA.
Every combination Murphy comparison in the original-primary contexts. Crossing prevents threshold-uniform sample dominance.
All three state groups for each original primary. The FX regression-minus-reference loss difference remains negative in every group, while the weekly evidence remains adverse.
Complete state diagnostic reference family. A joint rejection need not identify a useful state rule.
Complete target-level sensitivity. The lower-target directions recur, but upper-target evidence remains unavailable.
Every original quantile-regression horizon-coherence comparison. Ordered targets do not force ordered fitted reports.
Every threshold-crossing cell in the complete late diagnostic. A noncrossing elsewhere is not a calibration certificate.

Same-dealer daily sampled-position results; history and horizon count recorded nonempty calendar days. All methods share the declared evaluation grid; loss is scaled to USD millions for display only. The four-feature report yielding the isolated score gain has more breaches than its historical reference.

Six-step original regression across three inspected windows; the full-prefix window contains the earlier reported backcast, so this is not independent validation. Loss is scaled to USD millions for display; raw normal-HAC p-values are descriptive. Missing saved breach counts remain NA.

Complete full-prefix backcast comparisons; the two regressions use the original later-selected parameters. All planned comparisons are shown; raw normal-HAC p-values are descriptive. The window is already inspected and overlaps the earlier reported backcast.
Legacy calibrated simulation: all 24 planned cells.
First recorded failure in each unavailable legacy cell.
Pre-specified prefix stability diagnostics: all 15 source rows.
Complete source-by-arm conditional comparison, $W=52$.
Complete source-by-arm conditional comparison, $W=260$.
Corrected-rank F benchmark: all 52 source-by-arm-history cells.
Penalty-menu isolation on matched calibrated paths. Entries are the median relative loss (\%) across all 13 source medians, with the descriptive source IQR in brackets.

Paired penalty-menu isolation on unchanged calibrated paths. The expanded menu removes the large short-history full-regression loss in both arms. Longer-history full-regression summaries remain unavailable because a required repetition fails in each arm, with no successful-subset replacement.
Every menu-isolation source/arm/history/method cell. Relative-loss medians use all required repetitions.
FX original; method block 1/3. Full-grid $n=6625$.
FX original; method block 2/3. Full-grid $n=6625$.
FX original; method block 3/3. Full-grid $n=6625$.
FX early 2015; method block 1/1. Full-grid $n=1440$.
Treasury bills; method block 1/3. Full-grid $n=277$.
Treasury bills; method block 2/3. Full-grid $n=277$.
Treasury bills; method block 3/3. Full-grid $n=277$.
Other NYFed panels; method block 1/1. Full-grid $n=277$.
Same-record daily FX; method block 1/1. Full-grid $n=501$.
CFTC; method block 1/1. Full-grid $n=260$.

Accuracy and hit diagnostics for explicitly named reports. Panel A reports paired working-reference tests; Panel B uses the fixed nonoverlap grid for hit tests. A better average score does not imply fewer breaches.

Murphy diagram for the main short-horizon FX comparison. The full-breakpoint calculation finds crossings; the graph is a display of saved scores. Average pinball superiority does not imply dominance across elementary scores.
Murphy diagram for the main Treasury-bill comparison. The saved full-breakpoint comparison also crosses. A single average-score ordering leaves other consistent-score preferences unresolved.

Saved confirmation criteria for excess loss relative to matched historical headroom under additional synthetic innovation laws. Counts use the original fixed pooled denominators, including all counterexamples.
Ninety-percent model confidence sets across all planned comparisons. Counts retain their comparison or conditional-procedure denominators.

New York Fed validation-length comparisons on the unchanged evaluation sample. Entries are across-series median excess loss relative to corrected historical headroom, with changes in percentage points and selections of the ordinary empirical limit. Every method/horizon row contains all thirteen series.

Full-regression losses under short and long validation samples, with each reporting system retaining its own sources and histories. Points use unchanged evaluation origins; positive excess means higher loss than matched corrected historical headroom. The New York Fed short-horizon long arm also changes the validation endpoint and refit phase.
Historical fallback and adverse outcomes by source, horizon and training history. Counts use every planned comparison in each row; the last column counts protocol excess loss above ten percent.
